extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, their agents, and EPO examiners handling PCT Chapter II and supplementary international search (SIS/SISR) procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for handling Supplementary International Searches (SIS/SISR) and international preliminary examination under PCT Chapter II when the EPO acts as SISA or IPEA, including filing formalities, scope annex content, unity/non-unity handling, timing, and treatment of amendments/added subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope Annex (Rule 45bis.7(e)) — contents and citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Formally, the explanations under Rule 45bis.7(e) are part of the SISR (Form PCT/SISA/501) and are contained in an annex called the 'Scope Annex'. The Scope Annex will concentrate on the documents cited in the SISR, but in some circumstances it might be appropriate to raise objections based on documents cited in the ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a document cited in the ISR can be used as a Y document for inventive step for some dependent claims in the Scope Annex, it may be necessary to cite it again in the SISR as a Y document for those claims and provide argumentation in the Scope Annex. The examiner may choose to base objections only on documents cited in the ISR if expedient. If objections correspond to those raised in the WO-ISA from the main ISA, a mere reference to the WO-ISA objections will suffice. Examiners should generally avoid an explicit re‑evaluation or negative comment on reasoning given in the WO-ISA, keeping in mind differences in national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of priority and treatment of P/E documents in Scope Annex
rubrics_metrics.description: At the SISR stage the priority document should be available and can be checked for P/E documents found during search. If the priority document is not available, priority is assumed valid for the purposes of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If priority is not valid, this must be explained in the Scope Annex and any P documents found to be relevant will be dealt with in detail. If priority is valid, cited P documents do not need detailed treatment. Any E document which is a potential Art. 54(3) EPC document will be dealt with in the Scope Annex and the applicant should be drawn to its relevance (e.g. for the European phase).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying of documents cited in the SISR
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant will receive a copy of each document cited in the SISR free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Rule 45bis.6 and GL/ISPE guidance. Ensure applicant receives copies and that citations in SISR are documented to support applicant's ability to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-unity — general principle
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of non-unity only one invention is searched; there is no possibility to pay additional fees for further inventions under the SIS procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision as to which invention should be considered the main invention and thus searched is handled specifically in the SIS procedure (see GL/PCT-EPO B‑XII, 10.2). Where the main ISA has already objected to lack of unity, the applicant can indicate with the supplementary search request which of the inventions should be searched by the SISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deciding the main invention to be searched
rubrics_metrics.description: The main invention will normally be the invention first mentioned in the claims, but the examiner will exercise due discretion in selecting the invention to be searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may deviate if the first-mentioned invention is one for which no search report would be established or if the applicant requests that the supplementary search be limited to a different invention. See GL/PCT-EPO B‑XII, 10.3 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when the main ISA found lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: If the main ISA has already objected to lack of unity and the examiner agrees with the assessment in the main ISR, this can be reported by referring to the ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner forms a different point of view or agrees with a revised view on unity in a protest decision, the reasoning will be set out in full so it is easily understood. No reasons need be given why the lack‑of‑unity objection in the ISR could not be followed. If the examiner finds the application does not lack unity, a complete search is made for all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: When examiner disagrees with ISR classification (X/Y/A) — re-citation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner does not agree with some or all of the categories (X, Y, A) given in the ISR for documents he wishes to base objections on, such documents will be cited again in the SISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A‑documents found by the EPO as SISA will be cited in the SISR in any case. Use re‑citation to correct or change categorisation for purposes of the Scope Annex and SISR objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest / Review procedure for non-unity findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where lack of unity is objected to, the applicant has the right to protest; in the SIS procedure this protest is called a review. If the applicant requests a review he must pay a review fee; if no fee is paid the request is not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Review Panel (examiner responsible for file, an examiner chairperson and a further examiner) assesses arguments. The panel determines whether the lack‑of‑unity objection was justified on the basis of reasoning given in the SISR; the review does not include re‑evaluation to determine additional grounds for lack of unity. Outcomes: if objection unjustified → inform applicant with Form 503, no reasoning needed, reimbursement of review fee and corrected SISR established; if (partially) justified → Form 503 with reasoning addressing applicant's relevant arguments, fee not reimbursed, corrected search report if partially justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of SIS and Chapter II when EPO is European ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA was one of the European International Searching Authorities, the applicant can file a demand under Chapter II with the EPO and additionally a request for SIS by the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For such files the examiner will first establish the SISR with Scope Annex and then continue with Chapter II. Under Chapter II, a WO‑IPEA (Form 408) will be sent to the applicant if there are objections, since the WO‑ISA from another office is not recognised as a WO‑IPEA and the Scope Annex does not legally qualify as a WO‑IPEA (see GL/PCT‑EPO C‑IV, 2.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for international preliminary examination — form and filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand for international preliminary examination must be made using the prescribed form (PCT/IPEA/401). A demand selecting the EPO as IPEA must be filed with the EPO in Munich, Berlin or The Hague, by hand, post, facsimile or electronically; ePCT may be used for online filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO will indicate the date of receipt and promptly notify the applicant. If filed incorrectly with another Office/IB, that Office will mark the date and transmit the demand to the EPO. Time limit for filing the demand with the EPO is as defined in Rule 54bis.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence of the EPO as IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA receiving the demand should ensure it is competent to act as IPEA. The EPO is competent to act as IPEA only if the international search was carried out by the EPO or by specified other offices (AT, FI, ES, SE, TR, NPI (XN), VPI (XV)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure competence before accepting demand; see Euro‑PCT Guide for restrictions and specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the international application in the demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand must identify the international application by indicating the international application number, the international filing date, the title of the invention and the name and address of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Art.31(2), Rules 18.1 and 54 and Agreement EPO‑WIPO; ensure accurate identification to avoid processing defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant’s entitlement to file a demand
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand should contain name and address (including country) of applicant, state of nationality and state of residence. Sole applicants must reside in, or be a national of, a PCT contracting state bound by PCT Chapter II; with multiple applicants at least one must fulfil this requirement; the application must have been filed with a receiving Office bound by Chapter II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Rule 90, Art.31(2), Rule 54 and Euro‑PCT Guide points for edge cases and evidence of entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and deemed common representative
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand should indicate the agent or common representative appointed by the applicant(s) or a sub‑agent. Where an agent is appointed, correspondence will be sent to the agent's address. If multiple applicants and no common agent is appointed, all correspondence will be sent to the first‑named applicant who is considered the deemed common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate representative details on the demand (Art.37, Rule 53.7). Be aware of correspondence handling and consequences of 'deemed common representative' status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of states by filing the demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of the demand constitutes the election of all contracting states which are designated and are bound by Chapter II of the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure applicants understand that making the demand effects their election choices (Rules 53.8, 90.3(a), 90.4(a) and (b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for the demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand must be signed either by the applicant(s) or by the (common) agent or the common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Art.19 and 34, Rule 66; unsigned demands are defectives and may attract correction procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for international preliminary examination (as filed or amended)
rubrics_metrics.description: The preliminary examination is based on the international application either as filed or as amended under Article 19 or 34. The applicant must indicate on which basis he wishes the IPEA to start the examination (application as originally filed or with amendments), and may provide translations, comments about WO‑ISA (ISOREPLY) or about ISR, sequence listings, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 58.1 and 58.3. Fees for preliminary examination and handling fee must be paid. Clearly state the basis to avoid confusion about which text the IPEA should examine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of the IPEA file
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO as IPEA promptly establishes the file when conditions under Rule 69.1(a) are fulfilled, using the existing ISA file or creating a new file if the EPO was not the ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art.39(1)(a). Ensure file completeness and proper transfer of ISA materials where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of deficiencies in the demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA may correct certain defects ex officio; for others, the EPO invites the applicant to correct defects within one month of the invitation. If the applicant complies with the time limit, the demand is deemed to have been received on the actual filing date; if not, the demand is deemed not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art.31(3), Rules 53, 55 and 60. GL/ISPE references detail which defects can be corrected ex officio. Timely compliance is critical to preserve filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and refund of preliminary examination and handling fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the preliminary examination fee and the handling fee must be received at the EPO as IPEA one month from the date of receipt of the demand or 22 months from the earliest priority date, whichever expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules 57 and 58 and GL/PCT‑EPO A‑II for payment channels and GL for refund conditions (A‑II, 9.4 and 9.5). Late or missing payments can render the demand invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of the demand to the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The transmission of the demand to the International Bureau should be effected not later than one month after receipt of the demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules 61.1 and 90bis.4(a) — ensure timely transmittal to meet PCT processing timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute and rectified sheets treated as part of the application as originally filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement pages or sheets filed to correct defects (substitute sheets – Rule 26) or rectifications of obvious mistakes under Rule 91 are deemed to be part of the international application 'as originally filed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify such sheets with appropriate stamps ('SUBSTITUTE SHEET (RULE 26)', 'RECTIFIED SHEET (RULE 91.1)'). See GL/PCT‑EPO for procedures if rectified sheets contain added subject‑matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 20.6 sheets — missing parts or elements can be furnished later
rubrics_metrics.description: If parts of the application or an entire element (e.g., all description or all claims) were omitted, they may be furnished later without affecting the international filing date provided the missing parts were completely contained in the priority document and subject to Rules 4.18 and 20.6(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner checks whether the receiving Office's assessment of the 'completely contained' criterion was correct. See GL/PCT‑EPO H‑II for impact on the IPER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended sheets — consideration during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change other than rectification of obvious mistakes in the claims, description or drawings is an amendment. Unless withdrawn or superseded, any amendment must be taken into consideration for international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine amendments for added subject‑matter using same criteria as Art.123(2) EPC. See GL/PCT‑EPO H‑II and H‑III for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Added subject‑matter — examination and handling of claims with amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: All amended pages must be examined to see whether they introduce subject‑matter not originally disclosed, using the same criteria as under Art.123(2) EPC. If any newly filed claim, drawing or part of the description contains amendments considered to go beyond the original disclosure, the claim is examined taking into account only those technical features which have a basis in the application as originally filed, disregarding the offending amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examining only features with basis is not possible, the text of the claims as originally filed or amended under Art.19(1) is examined and reasons must be given on a separate sheet as to why the amendments introduce subject‑matter not originally disclosed and why they are disregarded (Rule 70.2(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter II general procedure — treatment of replies to WO‑ISA/WO‑IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Chapter II, the reply to the WO‑ISA, WO‑IPEA (Form 408) or telephone minutes with possible amendments will be examined. The examiner will first consider whether objections raised in the WO‑ISA have been overcome by submitted arguments and/or amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If objections are overcome and top‑up search does not yield pertinent prior art, IPER will be issued directly. If objections remain or new pertinent art is found in top‑up search, a further WO‑IPEA or telephone minutes should be issued. In some cases, minor amendments may be best handled via a short telephone consultation to achieve a positive IPER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispatch of a further written opinion (WO‑IPEA) when EPO was not the ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the ISR and WO‑ISA were established by another European ISA, the WO‑ISA is not considered the first written opinion for Chapter II and the examiner will examine the file and, if there are objections to novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability, send a WO‑IPEA with a time limit (normally two months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If despite a timely substantive reply there are still objections (possibly from top‑up search), a further WO‑IPEA or telephone minutes are issued. Rule 66.1bis and GL/ISPE references apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispatch of a further written opinion (WO‑IPEA) when EPO was the ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must be given a further opportunity for interaction in Chapter II before a negative IPER is established, on condition he has filed in due time a substantive reply to the WO‑ISA in the form of amendments and/or arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after reply objections still outstanding, the examiner must normally send a (further) written opinion (Form 408) or telephone minutes with a time limit to reply (normally two months), and attach documents newly found during top‑up search. If the applicant filed no reply and the top‑up search reveals no new pertinent prior art, a negative IPER repeating WO‑ISA objections may be issued directly. Exceptional rule: in a non‑unitary application where only unity remains as objection, a negative IPER can be sent directly without further WO‑IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account SISR by another office during Chapter II
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting preliminary examination under Chapter II, the examiner must also take into account any documents cited in any SISR by another office which is available in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the SISR has not been received by the EPO 24 months after the priority date, the file is sent to the examiner anyway; the examiner may send invitations to pay additional fees or WO‑IPEA as soon as possible without awaiting the SISR. If neither invitation nor WO‑IPEA needs to be sent before IPER, the examiner waits until 27 months to allow the SISR to arrive. If the IPER has not yet been established, the examiner will take the SISR into account when establishing the IPER (Rule 45bis.8(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Files arriving late — options and applicant consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the demand has been validly received by the EPO very late, the examiner will telephone the applicant, explain the situation, and offer options such as short telephone discussion/time limit for amendments, WO‑IPEA with short time limit, negative IPER without further interaction, or WO‑IPEA with a longer time limit (in which case IPER will be late).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant chooses no amendments and agrees to a negative IPER, the examiner will send a direct negative IPER. In exceptional cases where even short time limits would cause IPER after 28 months, the applicant is asked whether they prefer a time limit with a late IPER or a timely negative IPER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for a further written opinion by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants frequently request a further written opinion under Chapter II if the examiner’s opinion remains negative. If the applicant has not yet had a further opportunity to file amendments in Chapter II, his request must be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant has already had a further opportunity to file amendments, as a rule the IPER is issued directly. Follow GL/PCT‑EPO C‑IV, 2.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late‑filed replies after a WO‑IPEA — treatment depending on timing
rubrics_metrics.description: In PCT procedure there is no loss of right for late replies, but they may not be taken into account for the IPER. If a reply is received after the time limit but before an IPER has been started, the late reply is taken into consideration. If received after the IPER has been started and not all objections had been met, the late reply is not considered. If received after the IPER has been started and all objections had been met, the late reply is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 66.4bis and GL/ISPE 19.32–19.33. If no reply has been received, IPER is drawn up on the basis of the last WO‑IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of a restriction of the search for Chapter II examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the search covered only some claims or part of claims (restriction of search or declaration that no search is possible), only the subject‑matter which has been searched (as indicated in the ISR/WO‑ISA) can be the object of the international preliminary examination. It should always be made clear which claims have been examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a restriction or declaration of no search, the applicant’s reply may challenge the ISA’s findings, but the IPEA has no responsibility for actions taken by the ISA and there is no provision in the PCT for an IPEA review or appeal against such an ISA decision. Written arguments about completeness of the search are not to be treated as communication with the IPEA unless the reply contains a complaint against the findings at the search stage when the EPO acted as ISA (see GL/PCT‑EPO C‑IX, 4).
